references.text: Earlier in the chapter, Hosea, son of Nun, is mentioned as the representative of the tribe of Ephraim before Moses gave him the name Joshua.
Joshua is first mentioned as Moses' servant and commander in the battle against the Amalekites.
Joshua is referred to as Moses' servant when Moses went up on God's mountain.
Joshua, son of Nun, is described as Moses' young servant who did not leave the tabernacle.
Joshua, son of Nun, is mentioned together with Caleb as the two spies who brought back a positive report.
Joshua and Caleb were the only ones among the spies allowed to enter the Promised Land.
Joshua, son of Nun, is appointed as Moses' successor to lead the people of Israel.
Joshua, son of Nun, is mentioned together with Moses when they present the song to the people.
Joshua, son of Nun, is referred to as Moses' servant and takes over leadership after Moses' death.
Stephen mentions Joshua (Ἰησοῦς) as the one who led the people into the land during the conquest.
The book of Hebrews mentions Joshua (Ἰησοῦς) in connection with the rest that the people did not attain under his leadership.
